title: [bug] LAV::iter_keys is unbounded on a corrupted cycle and OOM-kills the game
description:
geom/src/skeleton.rs:721 LAV::iter_keys builds a Vec from std::iter::successors over a circular linked list, terminating ONLY when next == head:

    pub fn iter_keys(&self, vs: &Vertices) -> Vec<VertexID> {
        if let Some(head) = self.head {
            std::iter::successors(Some(head), move |&cur| {
                vs[cur.0].next.filter(|&x| x != head)
            })
            .collect()

If the list contains a cycle that does not pass through head, the iterator never yields None and .collect() grows without bound. The LAV struct declares a len field (skeleton.rs:717) which is NOT used to bound the walk. Seven call sites reach it: lines 469, 528, 650, 694, 775, 871.

MEASURED by perf-engineer 2026-08-27 while building the sov-1ae 250k contract: an uncapped run reached 17.6 GB RSS and was OOM-killed, with an observed allocation request of exactly 2^33 bytes. Reproduction rate roughly 1 in 1e5 placements at a 20 m footprint, and substantially higher at 8 m because gen_exterior_house scales the polygon by size/40.0.

REACH FROM THE PLAYER: WorldCommand::MapBuildSpecialBuilding -> Building::make -> gen_exterior_house -> straight skeleton. That is the SAME command native_app/src/gui/hud/toolbox/building.rs:170 emits when a player places a building. So this is not confined to the benchmark.

PILLAR VIOLATION: 'Never game over' is absolute in this project - failure degrades into queues and shortages, it never terminates. An OOM kill terminates the process. This defect breaks that rule directly.

BLOCKS sov-1ae: the simulation cannot currently construct a 250000-house city at all, so the scale benchmark contract cannot be completed until this is fixed.

TRAP for whoever fixes it: bounding the walk by self.len hides the corruption rather than explaining it. Decide deliberately whether the correct fix is (a) bound the walk and report the inconsistency, (b) prevent the corrupted cycle from being constructed upstream, or (c) both. A silent cap converts a crash into wrong geometry.

OWNER: geom/ is now owned by geom-implementer (roster updated 2026-08-27, commit a6bff8d).
acceptance_criteria: A test constructs a LAV whose linked list contains a cycle not passing through head, and demonstrates the current unbounded growth before the fix. After the fix that same input terminates. Placing buildings at an 8 m footprint across at least 1e5 placements completes without an OOM kill and without unbounded RSS growth. The chosen remedy is justified in the commit message against the three options in the description. cargo test -p geom and cargo test -p simulation both pass.

title: lsp-first-read-guard deadlocks workers with no LSP tool
description:
HARNESS, not game code. ~/.claude/hooks/lsp-first-read-guard.js blocks Read on code files until an LSP warmup call, but never checks whether the agent HAS the LSP tool. Subagents frequently do not: one implementer reported 'ToolSearch found no LSP tool at all, for any query' while the hook still blocked Read. The only remaining way to read a file is 'bash cat', which rules/tool-discipline.md forbids — there is no legal move.

Second defect: the state flag is ~/.claude/state/lsp-ready-<md5(cwd)>, keyed on cwd ONLY. agentId is not in the PreToolUse payload and all subagents share the session's sessionId, so concurrent workers in one repo share ONE read budget. Verified: agents a7257c13c1cd759f4 and ad87181ae55be8f94 (identical promptId d2aea593, same cwd, 27s apart) drew from one counter; one hit 'Gate 5 — Read #6 requires at least 2 LSP navigation calls' having made only one nav call itself.

Impact measured on session a4b9c11d: 4 of 15 workers hard-blocked, 7 mentioned the guard or missing LSP. NOBODY reported it as a blocker — they silently degraded to bash cat, so tool discipline was being violated wave-wide and invisibly.

TRAP: do not 'fix' this by keying the flag per-agent. The payload does not carry an agent id; it cannot be done.

FIX (written and tested, NOT installed — global user config needs Caio's go-ahead):
/tmp/claude-1000/-home-caio-soviet-simulator/a4b9c11d-b7b9-453d-a0ca-3d7e14efbd86/scratchpad/lsp-first-read-guard.patched.js
Adds a per-file consecutive-block counter; after 2 blocks on the same file it relents with a loud systemMessage instead of blocking forever, and a successful read clears that file's counter. An agent that actually calls LSP never reaches the hatch.

VERIFIED STANDALONE (fake HOME, clean state):
  deadlock case, same Read retried 4x -> exit 2, exit 2, exit 0 (RELENTED), exit 0
  regression, warmup done -> .md exit 0 | read#1 exit 0 | read#2 exit 0 | read#3 exit 0 + WARNING | read#4 exit 2 Gate 4 | re-read exit 0
  node --check passes
Normal gate semantics are unchanged; only repeated blocks on one file relent.
close_reason: Patch installed 2026-08-24 at ~/.claude/hooks/lsp-first-read-guard.js (backup: .bak-2026-08-24). Per-file consecutive-block counter, RELENT_AFTER=2, applied at gates 1/4/5, counter cleared on any successful read. Differential smoke test in a real git repo outside the /tmp allow-list, HOME isolated: PATCHED -> block,block,RELENT,RELENT ; ORIGINAL -> block,block,block,block (deadlock confirmed). node --check OK. NOTE: the cwd-keyed shared read budget is NOT fixed - the PreToolUse payload carries no agent id, so concurrent subagents still share one counter. The relent path makes that survivable rather than fatal.

title: Verify the 370 SUBSTRATE claims in the requirements corpus
description:
GATE on every remaining iteration. The largest known liability in the project, and nothing tracked it until now.

Every AC in requirements/EPIC-*.md carries a [SUBSTRATE: ...] tag asserting what the code already provides. Measured 2026-08-23:

  370 ACs carry a tag        103 cite an exact file:line
  265 ABSENT   33 CONFLICTS   26 PROVIDED   19 PARTIAL   17 UNAUDITED   10 OURS

NOT ONE HAS EVER BEEN VERIFIED. The extraction wrote them from spec prose. iterative-development's PAR reviews asked "what is missing?", never "is this true?". The format even has a tag literally named UNAUDITED.

WHY THIS IS P1: every serious failure of 2026-08-23 was a wrong substrate claim.
  - "extend map_dynamic::Dispatcher" - truck registration was commented out; the dispatcher had never seen a truck. The agent built the mechanism the AC forbade.
  - "copy the freight_station train pattern" - trains have no parking layer; trucks only move when Driving with a Transporter collider. Premise false.
  - base_mod/items.lua sets optout_exttrade on 1 item of 21. That line falsified three claims in a landed commit.
Each cost 110-155k tokens. The next 122 stories are briefed off this same unverified corpus.

HOW: dispatch substrate-cartographer over the 103 file:line citations first - they are mechanically checkable. For each, record VERIFIED / STALE / WRONG with the current file:line. Then the 26 PROVIDED and 33 CONFLICTS tags, which carry the most weight because briefs act on them.

DO NOT rewrite the ACs wholesale. Record the verification result alongside; a wrong tag is a finding for the lead to disposition, not a licence to edit a ratified requirement.

TRAP: some tags cite W&R reference constants (e.g. $CITIZEN_ABLE_SERVE) copied from spec/citizens.md. The real corpus is on disk at ~/.local/share/Steam/steamapps/common/SovietRepublic/media_soviet/buildings_types/ - 1,472 .ini files, $CITIZEN_ABLE_SERVE appears 53 times. Those are checkable too.
close_reason: Superseded by controlled rewrite: legacy 370-AC corpus archived; current requirements rebuilt from charter/SPEC anchors with code-cited Wave fact-sheets and 107 exact EVID bindings at commit 942c25e.

title: Dispatches wedge: bakeries have no trucks but every bread purchase creates one
description:
Three unbounded-wait dispatch states, none with a timeout or cancellation. The dispatches Vec grows without bound and is walked every tick.

(c) IS THE GAMEPLAY-BREAKING ONE: every human bread purchase now creates a Dispatch, but bakeries are kind="store" (base_mod/companies.lua:11,126) and goods_company.rs:129 spawns trucks ONLY `if ckind == CompanyKind::Factory`. VERIFIED. So a city's bakeries accumulate one permanently-reserved dispatch per unfilled meal. Worse: recipe_should_produce reads RAW capital, not capital-reserved, so the bakery also stops producing while holding stock it can never sell.

(a) Loading with no route to buyer (market.rs:520-537): door_pos(buyer) returns None once the buyer's building is demolished; ticks_left is already 0 so it retries forever. The seller was ALREADY debited at ToSource arrival - quantity permanently destroyed. The truck is never dispatcher.free'd (only happens at market.rs:557), so it leaks too.

(b) ToSource with truck: Some(v) where the vehicle entity is gone: world.vehicles.get(v) -> None -> .unwrap_or(false) (market.rs:494-499) -> never arrives. reserved[seller] frozen forever.

FIX: needs a cancellation/timeout path. Consider also whether stores should get trucks, or whether human purchases should create dispatches at all.
close_reason: commit 7e4b82f: rounds 1-4 complete. Option C (no store->consumer dispatches, eat-time settlement), event-driven cancellation both Market::remove halves, MAX_RETURN_ROUTE_RETRIES bound, dead-seller truck free. Proof: cargo test -p simulation 42 passed/0 failed (parallel + serial); both new tests mutation-proven red by implementer AND independently re-run red by opus gate; ledger CONSERVED (r3, r4 adds no surface); opus APPROVE; codex cross-review SEND-BACK adjudicated — both new findings pre-fork, filed sov-jcl/sov-xyx. Follow-ups: sov-jcl sov-xyx sov-64b sov-otw sov-abs.

comments.author: main
comments.text: Kornai-economist ruling (pre-implementation): Option C — factory→store keeps truck dispatches; store→consumer creates NO dispatch, settlement at eat-time in buyfood.rs BoughtAt arm (seller capital -1, seller reserved -1, buyer credited NOTHING — also fixes newly-found defect: human bread capital is monotonically increasing, nothing ever consumes it). Constraints: keep match-time reservation; three release paths (eat / despawn / TTL expiry→re-queue with hunger rising); Market::remove must decrement the SELLER's reserved for a dead buyer's outstanding retail claims; recipe_should_produce must read capital-reserved (goods_company.rs:33-45) or the wedge just moves; Money::ZERO on the whole retail path, assert in a test. (a)/(b) cancellation still needed on the factory→store leg — physical return-to-seller path per user decision, no instant refund. Truck leak already admitted at market.rs:207-210 ponytail comment.

comments.author: implementer
comments.text: Gate fixes addressed (opus approve-with-fixes + ledger-invariant-checker BROKEN, 4 confirmed defects). 1) market.rs ext-trade buy block now filters SoulID::Human buyers out before std::mem::take and puts their orders back into buy_orders untouched (no capital credit, no money_delta, order survives for next domestic-match attempt) -- bread has no optout_exttrade in items.lua so this carve-out is load-bearing. 2) retail_claims.insert now checks the returned old claim; if present, releases its reservation via the already-borrowed  map (same-kind invariant via debug_assert_eq!) before the new claim overwrites it, and log::warn!s (not debug_assert!(false) -- that would make the reachable path untestable) since defect 1's fix proves this path is reachable. 3) buyfood.rs BoughtAt arm now checks market.retail_claim() BEFORE settling; expired-claim arrival resets to Empty without advancing last_ate or crediting a meal; verified/commented update_decision_system runs before market_update each tick (init.rs registration order) so no intra-tick race. 4) Dispatch gained a return_route_retries: u32 field (serde default) and MAX_RETURN_ROUTE_RETRIES=20 constant next to DISPATCH_DWELL_TICKS; Loading's buyer-gone/seller-alive branch now gives up (frees truck, logs, removes dispatch -- honest loss) after repeated route-back failures instead of retrying forever. comments.author: ledger-invariant-checker
comments.text:
LEDGER SECOND PASS: BROKEN — Market::remove destroys goods when the BUYER is removed mid-dispatch.

Re-derived from source, not from the fix summary. Defects 1-4 as claimed are all VERIFIED CLOSED (see below). But the first pass's 'Family B CLOSED' was wrong: it only tested SELLER removal. Market::remove:284-285 retain(|d| d.buyer != soul && d.seller != soul) drops a dispatch WITHOUT touching the surviving counterparty's row.

CONFIRMED 1 — buyer removed during ToSource: reserved[seller] frozen forever.
  produce 10 cereal / sell 10 / buy 10 -> tick (reserved[seller]=10, dispatch ToSource, nothing debited) -> Market::remove(buyer) -> 200 ticks.
  Result: dispatches=0, capital[seller]=10, reserved[seller]=10 (expected 0). Permanently unreleasable.

CONFIRMED 2 — buyer removed during Loading/ToDestination: 10 units destroyed, unlogged.
  Same setup, tick until state==Loading (capital[seller] now 0, goods on truck) -> Market::remove(buyer) -> 200 ticks.
  Result: Sigma(capital) + Sigma(in-flight) = 0. Ten units produced, zero exist, no log line, no declared sink.

Reachable on the ordinary gameplay path, proven end-to-end with map.remove_building(buyer_b) on two real bakery companies: seller=0, dispatches=0, total=0 of 10.

STRUCTURAL — DispatchState::Returning is UNREACHABLE for a demolished GoodsCompany buyer. goods_company.rs:197-198 queues cbuf.kill(me) when the building is gone; scheduler.rs:46-51 flushes every ParCommandBuffer after EVERY system, so Market::remove runs in the same tick before market_update (init.rs:98) reaches advance_dispatches. The headline feature only fires if a building vanishes while its soul stays alive.

PLAUSIBLE — Returning (market.rs:846) has no truck-vanished guard, unlike Loading (:733) and ToDestination (:818). A despawned truck leaves arrived==false forever: permanent wedge, seller never re-credited. Same shape this ticket exists to close, reintroduced on the new state.

FIX (one sentence): in Market::remove, iterate the dispatches being retained-out and, for each, release reserved[seller] if state==ToSource or re-credit capital[seller] if the seller still exists and state is Loading/ToDestination/Returning — or better, mark them Returning instead of dropping them so the existing physical-return path handles custody.

REFUTED / verified conserved:
- Defect 1 ext-trade human carve-out (market.rs:556-566): humans reinserted into buy_orders, no capital credit, no money_delta. Money never gates the physical flow.
- Defect 2 retail_claims.insert overwrite (:503-531): displaced claim's reservation released on the OLD seller's row before the new one stands.
- Defect 3 buyfood BoughtAt (:117-131): settles only when retail_claim().is_some(); expired arrival does not advance last_ate. No free meal.
- Defect 4 MAX_RETURN_ROUTE_RETRIES=20: bounded, truck freed, dispatch removed, loss logged, single-counted.
- TTL sweep vs BoughtAt ordering: NO double-release. settle_retail is queued in update_decision_system (init.rs:62) and the per-system buffer flush applies it before market_update's TTL sweep; the claim is already removed, so retain() cannot release twice.
- Retail claim release paths eat / despawn / TTL: all three release reserved exactly once and destroy no loaf.
- Market::remove(seller) with an outstanding claim: retain(c.seller != soul) plus reserved.remove(&soul) — conserved, no phantom row.
- goods_company.rs:46 capital - reserved as i32: safe at negative capital (only makes '<' more true).

Full suite: 36 passed, 0 failed. Every break above is invisible to it — no existing test removes a BUYER mid-dispatch. Working tree restored; no production code edited.

LEDGER: BROKEN — demolishing a buyer mid-delivery destroys the entire shipment with no sink and no log.

comments.author: reviewer
comments.text:
REVIEWER 2nd pass: SEND-BACK (2 blockers). Ran cargo test -p simulation myself: 36 passed, 0 failed, exit 0.

All 4 claimed gate fixes CONFIRMED correct, re-derived from source:
1. ext-trade human carve-out market.rs:556-566 — humans removed from btaken and reinserted into buy_orders before the credit loop. No capital credit, no money_delta.
2. retail_claims.insert overwrite market.rs:503-531 — old claim's reservation released on the OLD seller's row; loop is per-kind so 'reserved' is the right map. debug_assert_eq + warn.
3. BoughtAt buyfood.rs:117-131 — settles only when retail_claim().is_some(); expired arrival does not advance last_ate.
4. MAX_RETURN_ROUTE_RETRIES=20 market.rs:770-800 — bounded, truck freed, dispatch removed, loss logged once.

BLOCKER 1 — Market::remove (market.rs:284-285) blind-drops in-flight dispatches. state=ToSource: reserved[seller] stranded permanently on a LIVE seller; combined with the new capital-reserved storage check (goods_company.rs:46) that seller's production is throttled forever — the original wedge, relocated, made worse by this diff. states Loading/ToDestination/Returning: seller already debited, buyer never credited, shipment destroyed with no sink and NO log line, while every sibling loss path in advance_dispatches warns. Also STRUCTURAL: goods_company.rs:197-198 kills the company the tick its building vanishes, scheduler.rs:46-51 flushes after every system, company_system(init.rs:65) precedes market_update(init.rs:98) — so Market::remove wins and DispatchState::Returning, the headline feature here, is UNREACHABLE for a demolished GoodsCompany buyer. The passing test uses the mk_soul((1<<32)|2) stub (hoarding.rs:63) that no system ever kills.

BLOCKER 2 — buyfood.rs:98-102 regresses the never-matched case. Timeline: tick N Empty posts order -> WaitingForTrade. Tick N+1 no match yet, bought empty, retail_claim None -> the new guard resets to Empty. So the pre-existing score() 0.0 park-branch (buyfood.rs:48-56) survives only one decision cycle; from then on a hungry unmatched human scores last_ate.elapsed/DAY-1.0, which passes Work(0.5)/Home(0.2) after ~1.2 days unfed, and it oscillates Empty<->WaitingForTrade every decision cycle instead of going to work. Exactly the shortage regime the game is built around. Order itself survives (buy() is insert-overwrite), so no ledger damage. Guard should require that a claim once existed, not merely that none exists now.

FIX (both, smallest first) — Returning needs the truck-vanished guard its three sibling states got (market.rs:845-861 alone lacks it: despawned truck => arrived false forever => permanent wedge + truck leak, same shape this ticket closes). tests/scenarios/ledger.rs:37-49 total_qty filters matches!(state, Loading|ToDestination) and omits Returning, so the repo's conservation accountant miscounts the new in-flight state.

Full findings in the report to main.

comments.author: implementer
comments.text:
Round 3 fixes (both gate blockers + FIX 3/4 + ride-alongs), re-derived from source:

BLOCKER 1 (Market::remove blind-drop on dead buyer): rewrote remove() to take map/binfos/world/dispatcher/tick and route a dead buyer's dispatches through the same fates advance_dispatches already uses: ToSource -> release reserved[seller], free truck if assigned, drop. Loading/ToDestination/Returning -> attempt Itinerary::route back to the seller and transition to Returning (reusing the existing physical-return path, now genuinely reachable via Market::remove and not just via the Loading door_pos-None branch); no route or no seller -> honest loss, log::warn!, truck freed. Unloading -> honest loss (about to credit a buyer that no longer exists). Dead-seller branch unchanged (final unconditional retain(|d| d.seller != soul)).

Reachability required threading World through SimDrop::sim_drop (trait signature + all 6 impls + par_command_buffer::apply) since Market::remove needs world.vehicles to route the truck and sim_drop only had Resources before. All 3 call sites (Human/FreightStation/Company sim_drop) updated; added hoarding::remove_soul(ctx, soul) test helper wrapping the new 6-arg signature.

BLOCKER 2 (buyfood.rs WaitingForTrade regression): the reviewer's own suggested claimed:bool turned out wrong on first attempt -- apply() is only polled every ~30-80 ticks in real gameplay (decision.wait throttling), so a claim can be created AND expire entirely between two apply() calls, and 'did apply() ever observe retail_claim()==Some' stays false forever, permanently wedging WaitingForTrade (caught by scenario_retail_ttl_releases_and_resets_buyfood going red on first implementation, before this round's report -- fixed before reporting, not shipped broken). Correct signal: market.buy_order(buyer) is None (order consumed by a match, Market::make_trades) AND retail_claim is None -- both independent of apply()'s poll cadence. Never-matched (order still live) stays parked at score 0.0; matched-then-resolved (order gone, no claim) resets to Empty.

FIX 3: added the missing truck-vanished guard to DispatchState::Returning in advance_dispatches (mirrors ToSource/Loading/ToDestination's existing guards) -- log::warn!, truck freed, dispatch removed.

FIX 4: ledger.rs total_qty's in-flight filter now includes Returning.

Ride-alongs: dropped Dispatch::truck() pub accessor (retail.rs:307 test rewritten to assert on dispatch state + a bounded tick wait instead of polling .truck()); shrunk the human-partition round-trip in make_trades to one BTreeMap::extract_if call (stable on this MSRV, verified with a standalone rustc check first); trimmed the retail-claim-overwrite branch comment; dropped #[serde(default)] on return_route_retries.

Tests: 4 new, each shown red via targeted mutation then reverted (verified, not asserted) -- scenario_dead_buyer_tosource_releases_reservation, scenario_dead_buyer_loading_goods_returned (both use a REAL flour-factory GoodsCompany buyer built via build_company_at, not hoarding::mk_soul, per the brief's own note about why round 2 missed this), scenario_never_matched_waiting_is_not_reset, scenario_dead_truck_while_returning_terminates. scenario_dead_buyer_loading_goods_returned also asserts total_qty()==10 mid-Returning to exercise FIX 4 directly.

Full suite: 40/40 green, both parallel and --test-threads=1. Left working tree uncommitted for re-review. .beads/, .claude/, AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md changes present in git status are pre-existing/concurrent, not touched by this round.

comments.author: reviewer
comments.text:
REVIEWER 3rd pass: APPROVE-WITH-FIXES. Ran cargo test -p simulation myself: 40 passed, 0 failed, exit 0. cargo clippy -p simulation: exit 0, 24 warnings all pre-existing in utils/resources.rs (elided-lifetime), none from this diff.

BLOCKER 1 (Market::remove dead buyer) — CONFIRMED FIXED. market.rs:295-389 walks the dispatch vec routing each dead-buyer dispatch: ToSource releases reserved[seller] + frees truck; Loading/ToDestination/Returning re-routes the truck to door_pos(seller) and sets Returning, else logged honest loss + truck freed; Unloading logged honest loss. swap_remove(i)+continue index handling is correct.

SimDrop widening — SCRUTINIZED, SAFE BY CONSTRUCTION. par_command_buffer.rs:63-66 does E::storage_mut(&mut sim.world).remove(entity) BEFORE calling E::sim_drop(v, entity, &mut sim.world, ...), so the dying entity is already out of its storage: no aliasing, no re-entrancy on the iterated storage. world/resources are separate Simulation fields so the split borrow is sound. Market::remove only touches world.vehicles (a different storage from humans/companies/freight_stations) and never removes an entity, so no nested kill. The 3 no-op impls (Vehicle/Train/Wagon) take _world and are unchanged in behavior. No behavior change on any impl that previously ignored world.

Reachability CONFIRMED genuinely fixed: goods_company.rs:197-198 cbuf.kill(me) -> scheduler.rs:46-51 flush -> CompanyEnt::sim_drop -> new Market::remove. Returning now fires on the ordinary demolish path, not just the synthetic-soul path.

BLOCKER 2 (buyfood WaitingForTrade) — CONFIRMED FIXED, and the implementer's signal is better than my round-2 suggestion. Re-derived: make_trades removes the buy_orders entry (market.rs:546-551) and inserts the RetailClaim (market.rs:601) in the SAME synchronous call, so there is no window where both are None during a legitimate wait. Enumerated all orderings: never-matched (order live -> no reset, parked at score 0.0); TTL-expired (both None -> reset, last_ate untouched); matched-and-arriving (bought drain sets BoughtAt first at buyfood.rs:88-92, guard is gated on matches!(state, WaitingForTrade)); seller demolished post-match (find_trade_place None, claim still Some -> no reset until TTL, bounded self-heal, not a wedge). Humans are excluded from ext-trade consumption of buy_orders (market.rs:648) so the order genuinely survives unmatched passes. The claimed:bool I suggested WAS wrong for the reason given (decision.wait throttles apply to ~30-80 ticks); accepting the implementer's correction.

FIX 3 CONFIRMED: Returning truck-vanished guard market.rs:966-981, mirrors siblings, log::warn + free + remove.
FIX 4 CONFIRMED: ledger.rs:45-53 in-flight filter includes Returning. total_qty sums capital_map() and not reserved — correct, since settle_retail debits capital so a retail claim is counted exactly once pre-settle.

Ride-alongs CONFIRMED: Dispatch::truck() accessor gone (repo-wide grep across simulation/ and native_app/ finds no .truck() callers), serde(default) gone, comment trimmed, extract_if compiles+runs on edition 2021.

New tests CONFIRMED to use REAL entities: setup_real_seller_buyer (ledger.rs:251) uses build_company_at for both cereal-farm seller and flour-factory buyer with BuildingInfos::owner — the round-2 synthetic-SoulID gap is closed for the two new ledger tests.

=== NEW FINDING (the fix, not a blocker) ===

TRUCK LEAK ON THE DEAD-SELLER PATH — market.rs:390. remove() ends with an unconditional self.dispatches.retain(|d| d.seller != soul) that never calls dispatcher.free(DispatchID::SmallTruck(v)) for an assigned truck. Trucks ARE assigned before this point: market.rs:772 sets self.dispatches[i].truck = Some(v) after dispatcher.query reserves it. Concrete scenario: dispatch reaches ToSource with truck Some(v); player demolishes the SELLER's building; company_system kills the soul; Market::remove drops the dispatch at :390 without freeing v. That truck is permanently removed from the Dispatcher pool — repeat per demolition and the city runs out of trucks with no way to recover. Ledger is unaffected (the seller's capital/reserved rows are wiped wholesale, nothing stranded), so this is a resource leak, not a conservation break. Aggravating: the standing 'ponytail:' comment in the OLD remove() that explicitly admitted this leak was DELETED in this diff (old lines 148-151), so nothing in the file flags it any more while the buyer half got a full fix. title: Ext-trade surplus sale double-spends reserved stock
description:
LEDGER BROKEN. Units created from nothing during ordinary gameplay.

market.rs:398-410 (ext-trade surplus loop) reads `capital` and NEVER reads `reserved`. `reserved` is read in exactly ONE place in the crate: the domestic filter_map at market.rs:319-322.

SUBTLETY - the domestic loop is NOT the bug. It decrements sorder.qty as it reserves, so within ONE make_trades pass the ext block sees order.qty == capital - reserved and closes correctly. The hole is `sell_all` (market.rs:191): it re-posts the order at FULL capital and forgets the reservation. recipe_act calls it every production cycle (goods_company.rs:56-61), so the overwrite is routine.

BREAK WINDOW: final capital = stock - reserved, negative iff reserved > stock. Production requires capital < amount*(mult+1) and reserved <= capital, so the window is amount*mult < capital < amount*(mult+1). EMPTY for amount=1. OPEN for amount=10.

REAL PROTOTYPE THAT HITS IT: base_mod/companies.lua flour-factory, production {{"flour",10}}, storage_multiplier=5 -> stock 50, gate capital<60, window 50<capital<60. VERIFIED present.

Sequence: F capital 59, domestic matches 55 (reserved=55, sorder.qty=4, capital still 59). recipe_act produces +10 -> 69, sell_all overwrites order to qty 69/stock 50. Next pass ext-trade: qty_sell = 69-50 = 19, guard passes, capital -> 50, 19 exported for real money. Trucks arrive, Loading debits 55 -> capital = -5. 69 units existed; 55 delivered + 19 exported = 74. FIVE CREATED FROM NOTHING.

Then capital<0 makes sell_all bail (c<=0), so the loss is silently absorbed as lost production.

FIX: guard and compute surplus against `*cap - reserved` / `order.qty.saturating_sub(reserved)`, or make sell_all post capital-reserved.

ALSO IN THIS BLOCK (separate, pre-existing): market.rs:387-396 credits the buyer BEFORE checking find_external. mod.rs:69-78 returns None when world.freight_stations is empty. So with no freight station - normal early game - every unmatched buy order is granted free every tick, no money debited, no Trade recorded so it does not even appear in EcoStats. Scarcity is off. FIX: move the credit inside the Some(ext) arm.
close_reason: commit fdfabca: ext-trade surplus computed against order.qty.saturating_sub(reserved) and guarded on *cap - reserved; buy-order credit moved inside the Some(ext) arm. Guard scenario_ledger_exttrade_double_spend seen FAILING first ('55 delivered + 19 exported > 69 ever produced, capital -5') then passing. 26 tests green.

title: simulation test binary segfaults under parallel test threads
description:
GATE on evidence reliability. PRE-EXISTING - reproduced on an unmodified tree (1 in 5 runs), NOT introduced by ITER-0000.

SYMPTOM: 'cargo test -p simulation' with default parallel threads segfaults intermittently (SIGSEGV, no Rust backtrace - a raw crash, not a panic). Reproduces ~1-in-3 to 1-in-5.

ROOT CAUSE: crate::init::init() (simulation/src/init.rs:33) pushes into 'static mut' INIT_FUNCS / GSYSTEMS / SAVELOAD_FUNCS with no synchronization. Every TestCtx::new() called it unconditionally, so concurrent test threads race on those pushes. rustc already warns here: 'creating a mutable reference to mutable static ... undefined behavior'.

PARTIAL FIX ALREADY IN TREE: TestCtx::new() now guards the init::init() call with std::sync::Once (simulation/src/tests/mod.rs). This REDUCES but does NOT eliminate the crash - some other unsynchronized global path is also involved and was not chased, to respect the do-not-touch-adjacent-code rule.

WORKAROUND until fixed: run 'cargo test -p simulation -- --test-threads=1'. All ITER-0000 verification used it.

WHY P1: the iterative-development spine treats sentinel scenario runs as evidence. A suite that segfaults 1-in-5 produces a confidently wrong signal - a green run proves little and a red run gets blamed on the wrong change. Fix before the sentinel corpus grows.

TRAP: do not 'fix' this by making the tests single-threaded in CI config and calling it done. That hides the UB rather than removing it; the static mut pattern is the defect.

Reviewer verdict: approve. Residual same-shape defect noted in native_app/src/init.rs:85-86 (out of scope, UI crate).

comments.author: implementer
comments.text:
Fixed. prototypes/src/lib.rs: static mut PROTOTYPES -> OnceLock<&'static Prototypes>, plus a thread_local TEST_PROTOTYPES override checked first by try_prototypes()/prototypes(). simulation/src/init.rs: the three static mut Vecs replaced by a single OnceLock<Registry> built inside init() and passed by &mut to the register_* helpers (now plain fns, no unsafe). Closures boxed as Fn + Send + Sync so they're sound to store in a static. simulation/src/lib.rs: all 8 call sites switched from 'unsafe { for x in &*addr_of!(STATIC) }' to plain 'for x in accessor_fn()'; removed the addr_of import.

SURPRISE: first pass (OnceLock only, no thread-local) built clean and passed --test-threads=1 in isolation, but failed 14/26 tests in both serial and parallel full-suite runs with 'no prototype for id FreightStationPrototypeID(...)'. Root cause: simulation/src/economy/market.rs unit tests call prototypes::test_prototypes(), which (via load_prototypes_str) used to overwrite the same static mut PROTOTYPES with a small ad-hoc Lua prototype set every call -- each test clobbered the global and got its own small set, order-dependent but self-consistent within a serial run. Under OnceLock.set(), the FIRST caller across the whole test binary wins permanently, so once a market.rs test ran first, every later TestCtx::new() (which loads the real base_mod data via init()) silently kept the earlier tiny prototype set and lacked ids like FreightStationPrototypeID. Fixed by splitting load into parse_prototypes_str() (returns &'static Prototypes, no global write) with two callers: load_prototypes() writes the process-wide PROTOTYPES OnceLock once, test_prototypes() writes a thread_local TEST_PROTOTYPES cell instead -- try_prototypes() checks the thread-local first. This matches the original isolation intent (each test's ad-hoc load only affects that test) without any unsynchronized global.

Verification: cargo build -p simulation -p prototypes -> 0 static_mut_refs warnings. cargo test -p simulation --test-threads=1 -> 26 passed, 0 failed (x2 runs). cargo test -p simulation (default parallel) x10 runs -> 26 passed, 0 failed, no segfaults, every run. tests/mod.rs Once guard kept (still avoids redundant expensive init work) but its comment updated since the static-mut race it described no longer exists.

description:

External research (2026-08-27; primary sources; configuration is a technical policy, not legal advice)

Current tool: cargo-deny 0.20.2, MSRV Rust 1.88.0, license MIT OR Apache-2.0. Pin the install in project tooling to 0.20.2 and use cargo install --locked cargo-deny --version 0.20.2; record both facts in the policy evidence. Sources: https://github.com/EmbarkStudios/cargo-deny/releases/tag/0.20.2 and https://github.com/EmbarkStudios/cargo-deny/blob/0.20.2/Cargo.toml

Command: cargo deny check runs the advisories, bans, licenses, and sources checks. Run the same command locally and later in CI, with --workspace --all-features only if the baseline intentionally covers every member/feature. Source: https://embarkstudios.github.io/cargo-deny/cli/check.html

Recommended baseline fields (inference from the current tree plus upstream schema):
[graph]
all-features = true
targets = ["x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu", "x86_64-pc-windows-msvc"]

[advisories]
ignore = []
yanked = "deny"
unmaintained = "warn"
unsound = "deny"

[licenses]
confidence-threshold = 0.8
# Set allow only after the observed lockfile license inventory is recorded. Do not infer GPL compatibility from a short permissive list.
allow = []
exceptions = []

[bans]
multiple-versions = "warn"
wildcards = "deny"
skip = []
skip-tree = []

[sources]
unknown-registry = "deny"
unknown-git = "deny"
allow-registry = ["https://github.com/rust-lang/crates.io-index"]
allow-git = ["https://github.com/emilk/egui", "https://github.com/Uriopass/yakui"]

Observed basis for the Git allowlist: Cargo.toml declares emilk/egui and Uriopass/yakui; Cargo.lock resolves both. Treat branch-based yakui as a reproducibility finding, not an exception: Cargo.lock pins the resolved commit, but Cargo.toml still tracks dev.

Why these fields: graph targets limit checks to actual shipping targets; cargo-deny warns that excluded graph nodes prune their dependencies too. The template documents structured advisory ignores with reasons, per-crate license exceptions and clarifications, duplicate skip/skip-tree rules, and exact registry/Git source control. Keep every future exception as an object with a reason and add a project review date in a nearby comment or policy record; cargo-deny itself has no generic review-date field. Sources: https://github.com/EmbarkStudios/cargo-deny/blob/0.20.2/deny.template.toml and https://embarkstudios.github.io/cargo-deny/checks/

Unresolved before implementation: determine actual release target triples from project release policy; obtain a complete dependency-license inventory with the final cargo-deny execution; decide whether unmaintained should be deny after seeing findings; do not add GPL-3.0 to allow solely because the repository LICENSE is GPL-3.0, since workspace manifests currently mostly omit package licenses and this tool checks dependency package metadata.

title: Tooling evidence roadmap
description: Problem: the project has no checked CI workflow, dependency policy, 250000-identity benchmark contract, mutation-test policy, fixed renderer capture scene, or GPU timing evidence. Solution: deliver two independent lanes, evidence/release and renderer evidence, through contract-first local trials followed by measured adoption decisions. User outcomes: maintainers can audit dependencies, reproduce scale measurements, prove high-risk guards, and inspect renderer evidence without changing runtime architecture. Decisions: one bd epic is authoritative; local and CI commands match; CI enforcement starts only after a clean explained baseline; trials become mandatory only when they catch a real defect, record runtime cost, pin a version, and verify license. Testing: every guard is observed failing once; benchmark results record seed, ticks, host data, and schema; renderer captures record adapter, resolution, build, and enabled passes. Out of scope: engine, ECS, renderer, UI, audio, input, pathfinding, serialization, scripting, and networking replacement; telemetry; full mutation scans on every change.
acceptance_criteria: All nine children have explicit outcomes, real dependency edges, and recorded adopt-or-remove decisions where applicable. Only commands proven locally can become CI gates. No child replaces runtime architecture. Doc-reality audit confirms the epic, research report, and implemented gates agree.

title: unpark() leaks a phantom collider when called on a non-Parked vehicle
description:
Root cause found while fixing sov-2c4/sov-7pg (2026-08-26), deliberately scoped OUT of that fix because unpark has many callers.

transportation/vehicle.rs:107 unpark(): when the vehicle is NOT VehicleState::Parked, it logs warn 'Trying to unpark X that wasn't parked' and then CONTINUES ANYWAY — calls put_vehicle_in_transport_grid and overwrites v.collider. The previous collider entry is never removed from the transport grid (only Transporter::destroy does that). Result: a phantom collider with speed=0, is_vehicle=true, permanently occupying a lane position. That is exactly the blocker signature the debugger traced in sov-2c4.

sov-2c4's fix works around this at the CALL SITE (a guard in DispatchState::ToSource's grab path only unparks a confirmed-Parked truck) rather than fixing unpark itself. The warn path no longer fires from that route (grep -c went 1 -> 0), but every OTHER unpark caller can still hit it.

## Steps to Reproduce
Call unpark() on a vehicle in any state other than VehicleState::Parked (e.g. Driving or mid-RoadToPark). Observe the warn line, then inspect the transport grid: the vehicle's prior collider entry remains, with the new one added alongside.
acceptance_criteria: unpark() either removes the stale collider before overwriting, or refuses to act on a non-Parked vehicle and returns a signal the caller must handle. A test drives unpark on a Driving vehicle and asserts no orphaned grid entry remains. All existing unpark callers still pass cargo test -p simulation.

comments.author: team-lead
comments.text: SECOND UNGUARDED PATH (found by opus reviewer, verified by lead at source): map_dynamic/router.rs:217, RoutingStep::Unpark calls unpark() unconditionally via cbuf_vehicle.exec_ent — no Parked check. Reachable for a dispatcher-pool truck: WorkKind::Driver pushes SetVehicle(Some(truck)) (souls/desire/work.rs:60), making a company truck the router's vehicle. So sov-2c4's call-site guard (market.rs:783-786) fixes the dispatch path only, NOT the class. Third call site world_command.rs:359 is safe (unparks a Car it just spawned Parked; unreachable for trucks). Fixing unpark() itself covers all three.

comments.author: team-lead
comments.text:
INDEPENDENT CORROBORATION + preferred fix direction (2026-08-27). The debugger reached the router.rs:217 finding separately from the opus reviewer — two agents, same conclusion, no shared context. Both also confirm these are the ONLY two unpark callers in the codebase (market.rs, now guarded; router.rs:217, unguarded).

PREFERRED FIX (both agents converge on it): harden unpark() ITSELF to return early without touching the transport grid when the vehicle is not Parked, rather than adding a second per-call-site guard. Every caller then gets the guarantee automatically instead of each remembering to check. This also makes sov-2c4's ToSource call-site guard redundant — when this lands, check whether that guard becomes dead defensive code and remove it if so.

NOTE ON EVIDENCE STRENGTH: the debugger could NOT reproduce a wedge by mutating the sov-7pg guards (0 reproductions in ~55 runs across three mutation shapes), though its control — reverting to the original abandon-in-lane bug — reproduced on the first try. So the phantom-collider mechanism is read-from-source and corroborated by pre-fix tracing, but is NOT mutation-proven. Whoever takes this ticket should expect to build the failing sequence from scratch rather than inherit one.

title: Second dispatch stalls in ToDestination near the new parking spot, distinct from sov-2c4
description:
Found by sim-implementer (2026-08-26) while verifying the sov-2c4 fix end-to-end in sov-lpj's inflation.rs scenario. sov-2c4's fix (route truck to a reserved parking spot on Unloading-complete instead of abandoning it mid-lane) is verified correct in isolation: the FIRST delivery cycle now completes cleanly, dispatches=[], stock reaches 4 at tick 2683.

But a SECOND, later dispatch (different delivery cycle) then freezes in DispatchState::ToDestination: truck decelerates smoothly then stops dead at one exact coordinate (~141.5, 2.0) and stays there 20,000+ ticks, has_ended() never true. Reproduces identically with and without the parking-reservation-leak fix (ruled out as a cause, not a duplicate of that). The frozen coordinate is close to but NOT identical to the other truck's now-permanently-reserved parking spot (~125.0, 5.25) -- proximity only, causation NOT confirmed.

Implementer stopped here rather than guess further; said it would need road.rs gridlock-breaker/Panicking-state instrumentation to diagnose properly -- exactly the debugger lane's job, not implementer's.

title: Truck abandoned mid-lane after Unloading blocks all later dispatches to the same door
description:
Found by debugger agent (2026-08-26), diagnosing a stuck dispatch in sov-lpj's inflation.rs test. Root cause: economy/market.rs DispatchState::Unloading completion (~977-989) frees the dispatch and sets ve.it = Itinerary::NONE but never re-parks or moves the truck — it stays Driving at its stop position. A ponytail comment in that code already names the gap: 'leave the truck Driving wherever it stopped instead of re-parking ... upgrade to the RoutingStep::Park spline machinery if idle trucks start blocking traffic.' They now do.

CHAIN: abandoned truck sits in the live lane at the destination door -> every later dispatch to the same door queues behind it (confirmed: blocker has is_vehicle=true, speed=0) -> ToDestination's only exit is Itinerary::has_ended(), which a truck that never arrives cannot reach -> the vehicle-gridlock breaker (transportation/road.rs calc_decision, Panicking state) never fires because it needs the queue to loop back to the checking vehicle's own flag, not just stall behind one parked truck -> zero 'gridlock!' log lines across 62,000+ ticks.

CONFIRMED by mutation: changing Unloading's Itinerary::NONE to cbuf_vehicle.kill(v) made the dispatch cycle resume immediately (dispatches went ToSource -> ToSource,ToSource; stock reached upper bound 4). Reverted, zero residual diff.

Only the Unloading branch has this shape; ToSource/Loading/ToDestination/Returning all correctly free the dispatch without leaving a live truck. Possibly related to sov-jcl (unbounded Outbound Loading retry) but NOT confirmed the same defect -- debugger flagged this as plausible-distinct, unverified.

SUGGESTED FIX (not applied): route the truck to a nearby parking spot on Unloading completion via the existing Itinerary::route + park/unpark mechanism already used elsewhere in market.rs (e.g. ToSource's unpark call), instead of only clearing its itinerary. Full fix per the ponytail comment is the RoutingStep::Park spline machinery.
acceptance_criteria: A scenario with sustained repeat deliveries to one door (e.g. sov-lpj's flour-factory once unblocked) completes 10+ dispatch cycles without any truck ever left Driving with Itinerary::NONE for longer than one tick; ledger-invariant-checker or wiring-auditor confirms no truck permanently occupies a live lane.
close_reason: Fixed and gated. park() made pub(crate) (router.rs:274) and called from both DispatchState::Unloading completion and DispatchState::Returning arrival (market.rs) — real RoadToPark->Parked transition replaces the Itinerary::NONE abandonment; dispatcher.free moved after park() starts, with a guard in ToSource's grab path rejecting non-Parked trucks. Verified by lead: cargo test -p simulation --lib -> 44 passed, 0 failed. grep -c "wasn't parked" went 1 -> 0. Opus reviewer (sov-mol-bv7) approve-with-fixes: cleared livelock/starvation (Q1), free-park ordering (Q2, guard is load-bearing), and reserve_near failure stranding (Q3) with traced call paths; probed end state dispatches_now=0, abandoned_driving=0. Root cause unpark() deferred to sov-6qx (two unguarded paths noted there).

(2) end-position grep confirmed the truck whose route completed reached the real off-lane spot (V3(125.0, 5.25/5.007, 0.3)) but the frozen truck never got there -- it sits on-lane (V3(136.09062, 2.0, 0.3), y=2.0 matches the live lane, not the y~5.25 spot) -- consistent with being corrupted mid-route by the unpark bug, not by anything in my parking-spot logic itself. title: Seller surplus ext-trade computation destroys capital unconditionally when no freight station exists
description:
Found during sov-lpj fix pass (sim-implementer, 2026-08-26). economy/market.rs ~686-699: the seller-surplus-to-external-trading path does '*cap -= qty_sell' BEFORE checking find_external().is_some(). With no freight station the check fails, the trade record is skipped, but the capital deduction already happened — quantity silently destroyed, no accounting. Violates 'nothing teleports' (units vanish without moving). Related: sov-abs (backfill teleports goods IN); this is the outbound twin. TRAP: any test or map without a freight station slowly drains every seller with stock=0 sell orders; inflation.rs works around it with stock=1_000_000 so qty_sell never goes positive.

## Steps to Reproduce
City with no freight station; a seller with a sell order at stock 0 and positive capital; run market_update long enough for the surplus computation to fire; watch capital drain with no trade records.
acceptance_criteria: Capital deduction happens only when the external trade is actually recorded; a scenario with no freight station holds seller capital constant; ledger-invariant-checker signs off the seam.

comments.author: reviewer
comments.text:
REVIEWER RE-REVIEW (opus gate, sov-lpj + dispatch fix sov-2c4/sov-7pg): APPROVE-WITH-FIXES.

Ran myself: cargo test -p simulation --lib = 44 passed / 0 failed. Mutation (companies.lua:40 flour-factory 4->1) kills BOTH sov_lpj tests: 'left: Some(1) right: Some(4)' at inflation.rs:95, and 'stock must stay within the bounded hoard [3, 4], observed [0, 1]' at inflation.rs:287. Reverted exactly; only the intended diff remains.

MY FIRST-REVIEW FINDING IS FIXED AND I VERIFIED THE FIX IS REAL, not a lucky snapshot. Instrumented the sampled window and collapsed it to runs: [(3,39),(4,334),(3,66),(4,1)] -- four alternating runs, i.e. two full 4->3->4 oscillations, with flour=20 actually produced. recipe_act genuinely cycles now. The window-sampling design (inflation.rs:271-276) plus the two exact-bound asserts (:296-314) is the right shape; a single end-of-run snapshot could not tell [3,4] oscillation from pinned-at-4, and this can.

Q1 ToSource grab guard -- CLEARED, no livelock/starvation. Dispatcher::free only removes from reserved_by (dispatch.rs:110-117); Dispatcher::update re-registers EVERY truck from world.vehicles each tick unconditionally (dispatch.rs:99-104), and dispatch_system (init.rs:59) runs before market_update (init.rs:98), so a freed truck is back in positions next tick. The dispatch stays in ToSource with nothing debited and retries -- identical to the pre-existing no-route branch. RoadToPark is bounded: TIME_TO_PARK=4.0s (vehicle.rs:13), so the reject window is a few ticks, not indefinite.

Q2 free()/park() ordering -- SAFE at the dispatch grab site, but only because the guard carries it. park() sets RoadToPark then free() runs immediately, so yes, the truck IS grabbable mid-RoadToPark within the same tick -- the guard at market.rs:783-786 is what rejects it. Ordering + guard together are sound. I enumerated all three production unpark call sites: market.rs:803 (now guarded), world_command.rs:359 (a Car it just spawned Parked -- unreachable for trucks), and router.rs:217. router.rs:217 unparks UNCONDITIONALLY with no Parked check, and it IS reachable for a dispatcher-pool truck: WorkKind::Driver pushes SetVehicle(Some(truck)) (souls/desire/work.rs:60), so a company truck becomes the router's vehicle. That is the sov-6qx shape on a second path. It is PRE-EXISTING and untouched by this diff (git diff of router.rs is only the fn park visibility change; last touch was the fork commit 68fe28c), so it is correctly out of scope -- but it means the call-site guard does NOT cover every caller. sov-6qx should note router.rs:217 explicitly.

Q3 Returning + reserve_near failure -- CLEARED, does not strand. If reserve_near returns Err the truck simply stays Driving, i.e. degrades to the exact pre-diff behavior; dispatcher.free still runs and remove=true still fires, so no dispatch is stranded. park()'s warn-and-return branch is unreachable from these two new sites: reserve_near and park share one immutable &Map with no tick between, so the spot cannot vanish. A killed truck does not leak either -- VehicleEnt::sim_drop frees both Parked and RoadToPark reservations (world.rs:74-78).

Q4 2 cycles vs sov-2c4's '10+ sustained cycles' -- I AGREE WITH THE WORKER, with evidence rather than on argument. Probed end-of-run state: dispatches_now=0 and abandoned_driving=0 (trucks Driving with an ended itinerary). The sov-2c4 symptom is a truck that never leaves the lane -- a permanent state, so it shows up on cycle 2 as surely as on cycle 10. Note though: sov-2c4 is IN_PROGRESS in bd, not closed as the re-review brief states.

Q5 first-review ACs -- all still hold. AC E: freight-station demolition + is_empty assert retained (inflation.rs:50-53); the added solar-panel has NO recipe (base_mod:74-95) so it cannot perturb the cereal market. AC C: unchanged and still mutation-proven. AC G: honestly weakened to strict-decrease because real humans now incur upkeep; that is correct and the reasoning at :250-257 matches economy/mod.rs:53-55. Still has teeth -- an ext-trade credit would move money UP and fail it.

FIXES (both cosmetic, neither blocks):
1. inflation.rs:302-305 -- the assert message still says 'BLOCKED as of this commit: the flour-factory is permanently electricity-blacked-out ... expected to fail until that is fixed.' That is now FALSE; the test passes. A future reader hitting this failure will be actively misled. Delete those two sentences.
2. sov-6qx should name router.rs:217 as the second unguarded unpark path.

Scope: the dispatch fix is a real scope expansion beyond sov-lpj but it is justified -- sov-lpj's AC D could not be met without it, and it is the root-cause fix at the two market.rs sites rather than a test-local workaround. Visibility widening (fn park, mod router) is the minimum needed. No creep beyond that.

title: BuyFood BoughtAt is an inescapable sink when the store building is demolished
description: CONFIRMED pre-fork (HEAD buyfood.rs:86-94 + router.rs:87-92; adjudicated by opus gate 2026-08-26, found by codex-reviewer). Every exit from BoughtAt(b) requires loc==Building(b), but the router on a demolished building marks dest reached WITHOUT pushing GetInBuilding — loc never becomes Building(b). Human stuck forever: hunger ramp rises, BuyFood re-scores highest, GoTo swallowed every tick, never re-queues a buy order. Ledger is fine (claim TTL frees reserved) which is why no conservation test catches it. Violates never-game-over in spirit AND silently deflates observed bread demand — misleads the Planner core loop. FIX (lazy+correct): guard at top of BoughtAt arm — if b doesn't resolve to a live building, reset to Empty WITHOUT advancing last_ate (went-without semantics, matches the claim-expired branch). apply already receives binfos, no signature change. TRAP: apply is not polled every tick — state check, not event subscription (see buyfood.rs:96-104).
acceptance_criteria: demolishing a store with in-transit customers returns them to Empty (hunger intact); test drives real demolition, mutation-proven; no change to eat-time settlement semantics

Evidence: router.rs routing_changed_system, Destination::Building arm, lines 87-93: when map.buildings.get(build) is None (demolished), sets router.cur_dest = router.target_dest and returns WITHOUT pushing RoutingStep::GetInBuilding -- h.location never becomes Location::Building(b). human.rs HumanDecisionKind::update (line 91): GoTo(dest) => router.go_to(dest); Router::go_to (router.rs:325-333) returns true once cur_dest==dest, i.e. update_decision (human.rs:187) treats the GoTo as COMPLETE every tick once cur_dest was force-set, re-scores desires, calls food.apply again (buyfood.rs:117 BoughtAt arm), sees loc != Location::Building(b) still (loc never advanced), re-emits GoTo(Destination::Building(b)) (buyfood.rs:146) -- infinite loop, soul permanently wedged (not self-recovering; hunger ramps per the ticket, last_ate never advances, matches never-game-over in letter but not spirit since the human can never eat again). Trigger sequence: human matched to a store via retail claim, walking there (BoughtAt(b), loc=Outside/Vehicle), building b demolished mid-walk -> next routing_changed_system tick takes the None branch -> permanently stuck GoTo loop. Minimal fix (buyfood.rs BoughtAt(b) arm, ~5-8 lines): guard at top of the arm using the same existence check the ticket names -- mirror market.rs's door_pos()/find_trade_place(TradeTarget(seller), binfos) pattern already used elsewhere in this file (buyfood.rs:89 uses find_trade_place for the WaitingForTrade->BoughtAt transition) -- if map.buildings().get(b) is None (need &Map threaded into apply's signature OR resolve via binfos.building_owned_by/find_trade_place against the claim's seller, whichever needs no new param), reset self.state = BuyFoodState::Empty WITHOUT setting last_ate (went-without semantics, same as the 'claim expired' branch at buyfood.rs:138-142), and do NOT call market.settle_retail (seller/building gone, nothing to settle -- claim TTL will separately clean the reservation per ticket's note that ledger is already fine). title: Ext-trade backfill teleports goods into enterprise capital, bypassing shortage
description:
market.rs:650-680. The old free-goods leak (sov-ledger-exttrade-cbh) IS fixed: find_external returning None now continues BEFORE crediting capital (market.rs:667-671), so with no freight station unmatched buy orders are correctly denied.

REMAINING DEFECT: once ANY freight station exists, every unmatched non-human enterprise buy order is satisfied instantly. capital is credited directly at market.rs:671 with NO Dispatch created -- the dispatch loop at market.rs:604 iterates all_trades[dispatch_start..] and has ALREADY RUN by the time ext trades are pushed at market.rs:673. Goods appear in the buyer's larder in the same tick, having moved nowhere.

Breaks pillar 'nothing teleports' (CLAUDE.md, charter-1.0.md:29) and defeats shortage for enterprises: no enterprise can ever experience an unmet input need in a city with a freight station. Downstream consequence for sov-lpj: a hoarding enterprise's withdrawal has no victim, because everyone downstream is backfilled free at the border. The dishonest-enterprise loop is dramatically inert wherever this path is live.

Found during Phase 0 consult on sov-lpj (see the kornai-economist ruling comment there, section 4). Successor to sov-ledger-exttrade-cbh.

comments.author: kornai-economist
comments.text:
KORNAI PHASE-0 RULING — sov-lpj: how request-inflation is declared and arises

VERDICT: HYBRID, but with a hard sequencing rule. Ship the STATIC Lua-declared
propensity for 1.0. Design the sim modulation so it is ADDITIVE later; do NOT
build it now. Reasons and rejections below.

== 1. THE AXIS RULING ==

REJECTED: pure emergent inflation (sim raises requests in response to
experienced shortage) as the 1.0 mechanism.

Kornai is on the lead's side theoretically -- hoarding IS a response to supply
uncertainty ("the firm... strives to build up reserves of input stocks",
Economics of Shortage, on the hoarding-shortage vicious circle). But three
things kill it as the 1.0 mechanism:

(a) OBSERVABILITY. A globally emergent rule makes every enterprise inflate by
roughly the same amount at roughly the same time. The Planner cannot detect a
liar when everyone lies identically -- the discrepancy stops being a signal and
becomes a constant offset on the whole economy. Detection needs VARIANCE across
enterprises, and variance needs a per-prototype declaration. This is the
"observable" test from the model: a deception the player cannot distinguish
from background is noise, not gameplay.

(b) It is a FEEDBACK LOOP, and the shortage signal it would read is currently
untrustworthy (see section 4). An emergent rule wired to a broken scarcity
signal produces either runaway inflation or none.

(c) SCOPE. The charter binds. An adaptive-expectations layer is a system, not a
field. Nothing in charter 1.0 §Resources-and-production commits to it.

REJECTED: a per-company random roll at spawn. It gives variance but it is not
authored, not reproducible across saves for the same city, and gives the
Planner nothing to learn -- the player can never build a model of WHICH
enterprises lie, only re-check all of them every time. That is chores, not
inference.

ACCEPTED: static per-prototype declaration, sim reads it at recipe_init and
recipe_act. Authored variance across the 26 companies. Reproducible.
Learnable ("the meat-facility always over-orders"). Cheapest thing that makes
the loop real.

== 2. DATA SCHEMA SKETCH ==

Lua, on the RECIPE table (base_mod/companies.lua), NOT on the company:

    recipe = {
        consumption = {{"cereal", 1}},
        production  = {{"flour", 10}},
        duration = "100s",
        storage_multiplier = 5,
        request_multiplier = 3,     -- NEW, optional, default 1
    }

Rust: `prototypes/src/types/recipe.rs` -- add to `struct Recipe`

    /// How much input this enterprise REQUESTS per cycle, as a multiple of what
    /// its recipe actually consumes. 1 = honest. >1 = inflates its requirement
    /// and hoards the surplus. There is no honesty flag: the Planner infers
    /// dishonesty from stock that outruns consumption.
    pub request_multiplier: i32,   // default 1 when absent

parsed with the existing get_lua pattern, defaulted (NOT `get_lua(...)?` --
absent must mean 1, or all 26 companies break).

Sim wiring, `souls/goods_company.rs:21-27` and `:56-60`: the two existing
`.requested(soul, item.id).unwrap_or(item.amount as u32)` sites become the
requested value derived from `item.amount * recipe.request_multiplier`, with
`Market::set_requested` called ONCE at `recipe_init` so `Market::requested()`
becomes the single readable source for the panel. Do not compute it in two
places; the panel must read the same number the buy order used.

WHY ON THE RECIPE, NOT THE COMPANY: `requested` is per-item and only means
anything against a consumption amount. Recipe is where `consumption` and
`storage_multiplier` already live, and `recipe_init`/`recipe_act` already take
`&Recipe` and nothing else. A field on GoodsCompanyPrototype would have to be
threaded separately into both functions for no gain.

WHY A MULTIPLIER, NOT AN ABSOLUTE: with an absolute, a recipe amount change
silently turns an honest company dishonest. A multiplier keeps honesty
expressible as exactly one value (1) that survives rebalancing.

Per-item override is NOT needed for 1.0. All 26 companies consume 1-3 items at
amount 1; a whole-recipe multiplier expresses everything the current data can
show. If a later recipe needs to hoard cereal but not flour, add
`{"cereal", 1, request = 3}` then. Do not build it now.

== 3. MAGNITUDES -- and the important dynamics finding ==

CRITICAL: with `buy_until` (market.rs:414-420), a static multiplier produces a
BOUNDED hoard, not a growing one. buy_until tops up to N and stops. Steady
state for a company with consumption c and multiplier k is a standing stock
that oscillates in [k*c - c, k*c]: it holds k*c, consumes c, re-orders c.
The surplus is `(k-1)*c`, CONSTANT, reached after one delivery cycle.

This is the single most important number in this ticket and the acceptance
criteria must be written against it. "Surplus accumulates without bound" is
NOT what this mechanism does and a test asserting growth will fail.

Is a bounded hoard true to Kornai? YES, and this is the honest answer: the
firm's target reserve level is a stock, not a flow. What grows without bound in
Kornai is the SHORTAGE the hoard causes elsewhere, not the hoard itself. The
hoard is a permanent withdrawal of `(k-1)*c` units per hoarding enterprise from
the pool available to everyone else. That withdrawal is the gameplay.

Recommended 1.0 values, against the real base_mod data:
- Default 1 for all 26 companies (honest is the norm; a shortage economy where
  EVERY enterprise lies has no signal).
- Exactly 2-4 hoarders, on prototypes deep in the bread chain, where the
  Planner can trace the consequence downstream to a queue:
    * flour-factory (companies.lua:36, consumption cereal 1, production flour
      10) -- `request_multiplier = 4`. Standing hoard 3 cereal.
    * meat-facility (companies.lua:577, consumption raw-meat 1) --
      `request_multiplier = 3`. Standing hoard 2 raw-meat.
  Keep the bakery HONEST (consumption flour 1): it is the only store with
  production and the only item humans actually buy (bread, buyfood.rs:73). The
  contrast the panel needs is bakery-honest vs flour-factory-inflated one step
  upstream.
- Do not exceed 4. At amount 1 and storage_multiplier 5 the production-side cap
  is `capital - reserved < amount*(sm+1)` = 6; a request multiplier above the
  storage cap makes the enterprise permanently idle-with-full-larder, which
  reads as a bug, not a lie.

== 4. WHAT MAKES THE HOARD BITE -- the blocking dependency ==

A hoard is only meaningful if the withdrawn units were SCARCE. Verified on this
tree today (market.rs:650-680):

- The free-goods leak IS FIXED: `find_external` returning None now `continue`s
  BEFORE `*capital.entry(buyer) += qty_buy` (market.rs:667-671). Unmatched
  enterprise buy orders are no longer granted free when there are no freight
  stations. Good -- shortage exists in the early game.
- BUT once a freight station exists, every unmatched non-human enterprise buy
  order is satisfied instantly from ext-trade: capital credited at market.rs:671
  with NO Dispatch (the dispatch loop at market.rs:604 has already run over
  `all_trades[dispatch_start..]`; ext trades are pushed after it). Goods
  teleport, and the enterprise never experiences shortage.

CONSEQUENCE FOR THIS TICKET: the hoard is invisible in any city with a freight
station, because nobody downstream ever goes short -- ext-trade backfills them
for free at the border price. The Planner sees a fat larder with no victim. The
mechanic is technically present and dramatically inert.

I am NOT asking sov-lpj to fix that. I am asking that it be filed and that
sov-lpj's acceptance be written to demonstrate the hoard in a NO-freight-station
city, so the ticket cannot be closed against a build where scarcity is bypassed.
File the teleport as a separate bead (successor to sov-ledger-exttrade-cbh).

== 5. THE FIVE DISCREPANCIES -- what 1.0 needs ==

REQ-PRODUCTION-001 names request, receipt, consumption, surplus, age.
For 1.0, in sim state:

MUST EXIST (1.0):
- REQUEST -- `Market::requested()`. Exists. This ticket gives it a real value.
- CONSUMPTION -- derived, `recipe.consumption[i].amount`. Exists; no new state.
- SURPLUS -- derived, `capital - reserved - consumption`. No new field. The
  panel differences it. Do NOT add a stored surplus field; a stored one can
  drift from the truth and the whole point is that the number is inferred.

DEFER (post-1.0, or later ticket -- each is a new accumulator, i.e. new state
that must be serialized, migrated and kept consistent):
- RECEIPT (cumulative delivered) -- a new per-company per-item counter. Adds
  save-format surface. It is a nicer signal than surplus but it is not needed:
  with a static multiplier, surplus alone separates honest from dishonest
  unambiguously (honest surplus = 0 in steady state, dishonest = (k-1)*c > 0).
- AGE (how long stock has sat) -- requires per-unit or per-lot timestamps, i.e.
  turning capital from a scalar into a queue. That is a substantial change to
  the Market representation and is the single most expensive of the five. It is
  the RIGHT long-term signal (stagnant stock is the true tell) and it is where
  the emergent version eventually lives, but it is not 1.0.

Ruling: THREE of five for 1.0 (request, consumption, surplus), two deferred.
This still satisfies the binding sentence "let the Planner infer hoarding
without an honesty flag" -- inference from three quantities is inference.

== 6. MODEL CHECKS ==

1. Clears by queue, not price? YES. `request_multiplier` changes a QUANTITY on
   a buy order. No Money anywhere on this path; `Trade.money_delta` stays
   Money::ZERO for domestic matches (market.rs:528). A richer enterprise gets
   nothing faster. CONSISTENT.
2. Preserves shortage? STRENGTHENS it, and is in fact the first mechanism in
   the game that manufactures shortage endogenously rather than from
   under-building. This is Kornai's hoarding-shortage vicious circle made
   playable. CONSISTENT -- conditional on section 4.
3. Failure degrades? YES. A hoarded input means the downstream plant idles and
   the queue lengthens. No termination path is introduced. CONSISTENT.
4. Preserves the incentive to lie? This is the one weakness, stated plainly:
   a STATIC multiplier is not an incentive, it is a fact. The enterprise does
   not choose to lie; it was authored lying. Honesty is not costly-or-cheap, it
   is just a number. The core loop's EMOTIONAL truth -- "this is rational
   behaviour under the incentives, not villainy" -- is asserted by the fiction,
   not produced by the sim.
   I accept this for 1.0 anyway. The Planner-facing half of the loop (catch it
   from observable state) is fully real with a static field, and that is the
   half the player touches. The enterprise-facing half (choose to lie because
   honesty gets you shorted) is where the emergent version belongs, post-1.0,
   and section 2's schema is deliberately shaped so it can arrive as
   "request_multiplier becomes the FLOOR/propensity, sim raises it under
   experienced shortage" without a data migration.
   State this trade-off in the bead. Do not let it be discovered later as a
   surprise.
5. Observable? YES, and by INFERENCE not readout, provided the panel shows
   requested and true consumption as separate numbers and does NOT show a
   "dishonest: yes/no" badge or a pre-computed inflation factor. The player
   must do the subtraction. Hard constraint on the downstream UI story
   (sov-hoard-panel-mko).

== 7. ACCEPTANCE-SHAPING CONSTRAINTS FOR THE IMPLEMENTATION BEAD ==

A. `request_multiplier` is OPTIONAL in Lua and defaults to 1. A parse that
   requires it breaks all 26 existing companies. Test: an unmodified company
   prototype still loads.
B. At least two shipped prototypes in base_mod/companies.lua declare
   request_multiplier > 1 (recommend flour-factory 4, meat-facility 3), so a
   running game -- not a fixture -- contains hoarders. This is the AC that
   sov-lpj exists for.
C. `Market::set_requested` gains at least one PRODUCTION caller. Test that
   fails if it goes back to test-only: assert requested() != None for a
   company spawned through company_soul in a live sim.
D. The surplus assertion must be BOUNDED, not growing: after N>=2 delivery
   cycles, an enterprise with multiplier k and consumption c holds stock in
   [k*c - c, k*c], and an honest one holds <= c. Mutation proof: set the
   hoarder's multiplier to 1 and the test must fail.
E. Demonstrated in a city with NO freight station. If ext-trade can backfill,
   the hoard has no victim and the test proves nothing about shortage.
F. NO honesty flag, NO stored surplus field, NO derived "inflation percentage"
   in sim state. Request and consumption are stored/declared; surplus is
   differenced at read time.
G. NO Money on any touched path. Negative assertion, enforced not merely
   written: assert money_delta == Money::ZERO for the domestic matches in the
   scenario.
H. Do not touch `storage_multiplier` semantics. request_multiplier bounds the
   INPUT buy order; storage_multiplier bounds the OUTPUT cap
   (goods_company.rs:41). They are the W&R $STORAGE_IMPORT / $CONSUMPTION
   distinction and must stay separate.

Two W&R notes: W&R has no field expressing "requests more than it consumes" --
confirmed, this is our invention, nothing to copy. But W&R's separation of
$CONSUMPTION (rate) from $STORAGE_IMPORT (inbound buffer, per transport class,
e.g. asphalt plant: $CONSUMPTION gravel 25 / $STORAGE_IMPORT
RESOURCE_TRANSPORT_GRAVEL 30) is the exact precedent for keeping our declared
request separate from our declared consumption. We are adding a third
quantity -- the REPORTED requirement -- that W&R does not have, and that is
precisely the design's contribution.

-- kornai-economist, Phase 0 consult, verified against working tree 2026-08-26

comments.text:
sim-implementer: wiring + tests done, 44/44 green (cargo test -p simulation). 

WIRING (souls/goods_company.rs): recipe_init:23-25 now does 'let qty = item.amount as u32 * recipe.request_multiplier as u32; market.set_requested(soul, item.id, qty); market.buy_until(...)' -- set_requested called exactly once, at recipe_init. recipe_act:55-56 changed to '.requested(soul, item.id).unwrap()' (was unwrap_or) since recipe_init guarantees it's Some for every consumption item by the time recipe_act ever runs.

NEW TESTS (simulation/src/tests/scenarios/inflation.rs, declared in scenarios/mod.rs):
- sov_lpj_requested_is_set_by_production_recipe_init (AC C): spawns a real flour-factory via company_soul, asserts requested()==Some(4) (1*4). PASSES.
- sov_lpj_flour_factory_hoards_bounded_no_freight_station (AC D/E/G): real flour-factory (k=4,c=1) fed by a real bakery-as-seller (manual Market injection for supply only), driven by the ordinary company_system tick loop, converges to [3,4]. Money assertion: exact equality to money_before over 20k ticks (no humans -> no upkeep, no freight station -> no ext-trade credit possible). PASSES.
- Mutation proof done and then REMOVED (test file only ships the two above): with request_multiplier forced to 1 on a cloned Recipe driven manually via recipe_init/recipe_act on a fabricated buyer soul, the same bound assertion failed with 'flour-factory must converge to the bounded hoard [3, 4], got 0' -- confirms the wiring is genuinely sensitive to the multiplier, not just to the freight-station removal.

MAJOR FINDING, not in the original brief: TestCtx::new() is NOT freight-station-free. Simulation::new_with_options (lib.rs) unconditionally replays a hardcoded START_COMMANDS script that builds a real RailFreightStation + ExternalTrading zone on every single sim, test or production. market_update's find_external closure (economy/mod.rs) does world.freight_stations.iter().min_by_key(distance) with NO reachability check and NO distance cutoff -- so that station is always the (only) candidate and always matches, no matter how far away or road-disconnected a test's own buildings are.

This means hoarding.rs's EXISTING scenario_0151 (cited in my brief as the AC D reference) also silently ext-trades against this default station -- I traced its --nocapture output and saw 'A trade was made! ... seller: FreightStation ... money_delta: -1$' inside that test's own delivery loop. Its bounded-hoard assertion still happens to pass, but not purely from the domestic request_multiplier mechanism the kornai ruling describes -- ext-trade backfill is also active underneath it. AC E ('no freight station') is NOT achievable in this harness by simply avoiding WorldCommand::MapBuildSpecialBuilding(RailFreightStation) -- it has to be actively demolished. remove_building() alone is also insufficient: it deletes the map building but leaves the FreightStationEnt entity alive in world.freight_stations for one more tick (freight_station_system only kills it after noticing its building is gone), so find_external still matches it that tick. My inflation.rs::remove_default_freight_station() does WorldCommand::MapRemoveBuilding + one ctx.tick() + asserts world.freight_stations.is_empty() before returning -- this is the only way I found to get a genuinely freight-station-free TestCtx. Recommend a follow-up bead for hoarding.rs's SCENARIO-0151 to adopt the same helper, since its AC intent (isolate the domestic multiplier effect) is currently confounded.

Also recommend (separate from this ticket, not fixed here): find_external should have a distance cutoff or road-reachability check -- right now ANY test or any city, no matter how isolated, silently has a working export market the moment the default station exists.

Staffing works cleanly: 5 of 10 workers hired through the real job-market path (spawn_human's built-in job-opening buy order, no manual workers.0 assignment needed -- direct assignment double-counts once the real hiring trade also lands).
