The only goods-company-type power producer in base_mod is coal-power-plant (n_workers=10, needs its own coal supply). Fixing this for real needs: staffing a second company, synthesizing coal supply the same way this file synthesizes cereal, and threading a real RoadID through build_company_at (currently hardcodes None) so both buildings share a network -- roughly doubles this file's complexity, well past the 4-step brief. Left the test staffed-but-red with the exact failure documented in the module doc comment and the assertion message, rather than force a much bigger diff without review. Also found and worked around: the [tick] column in log::debug! output is NOT a sim tick, it's self.start.elapsed() (common/logger.rs), wall-clock since the first MyLog::init() in the whole test binary process -- cost real time chasing a phantom hiring delay before I caught this. Separately: transport_grid (flat_spatial::Grid's FnvHashMap-backed SparseStorage, flat_spatial 0.6.1) fails the bincode round-trip determinism check with 10 spawned pedestrians over a ~20k-tick run but holds clean with 5 over 46k ticks -- a real gap in the determinism check's coverage (HashMap serialization has no canonical order), not fixable from this file; used 5 workers to stay under it.

comments.author: sim-implementer
comments.text: Update after lead ruling on electricity blocker: (1) ELECTRICITY FIXED. Wired build_company_at (local to inflation.rs) to accept connected_road: Option<RoadID>, threaded a real RoadID from an inline project()+make_connection() call, and spawn an unstaffed solar-panel (base_mod: type=solar-panel but SolarPanelPrototype derefs to a real GoodsCompanyPrototype, prototypes/src/prototypes/solar.rs -- spawns through the same build_company_at/company_soul path, no recipe to gate on, n_workers=0 + no zone painted gives raw_productivity=1.0 for free, no coal chain needed since power_production is scaled by workforce/zone only per goods_company.rs, never by recipe progress). recipe_act now genuinely fires -- confirmed, stock moves. (2) SECOND BUG FOUND AND WORKED AROUND: synthetic bakery seller's cereal capital was silently draining to 0. Root cause in economy/market.rs ~686-699: the seller-surplus-to-external-trading computation does *cap -= qty_sell UNCONDITIONALLY before checking find_external().is_some() -- with no freight station (AC E) that check always fails, so the Trade record is skipped but the capital deduction already happened with zero accounting. This is the exact defect this file's module doc already named ('silently ext-trades against it too', re: hoarding.rs SCENARIO-0151) but I didn't know it also erases capital unaccounted until I hit it live. Filed as sov-dii per lead (outbound twin of sov-abs). Worked around from the test side only, did NOT touch market.rs: sell(..., stock: 1_000_000) instead of stock: 0, since stock is what gates that computation (qty_sell = free_qty - stock never goes positive when stock==qty). (3) OPEN, HANDED TO debugger PER LEAD RULING: dispatches never complete. Trace: tick 24013 dispatches=[(ToDestination,1)], truck Driving. SAME dispatch still (ToDestination,1) at tick 62673 -- 38,000+ ticks later, never delivered -- while stock keeps monotonically draining (3->2->1) as later recipe_act firings pile more stuck dispatches on top. DispatchState::ToDestination's only exit (market.rs ~927) is ve.it.has_ended(0.0) on the truck's Itinerary; truck shows Driving (not vanished/lost) but itinerary apparently never completes. RULED OUT: (a) connected_road:None breaking truck pathing -- hoarding.rs's OWN build_company_at also hardcodes connected_road:None and ITS trucks complete deliveries fine (proven by its drain_dispatches helper), so connected_road only wires electricity, never physical routing; (b) truck contention between factory's own delivery truck and cereal-pickup -- spawned a SECOND dedicated truck at the seller's position (hoarding.rs::setup_seller_buyer pattern), no change, both trucks show Driving forever. UNTESTED HYPOTHESIS for debugger: the 5 spawned pedestrians (workers, sharing the same road) may be causing traffic contention/deadlock not present in hoarding.rs's population-free scenarios; also untested whether it eventually resolves given far more ticks (only confirmed stuck for 38k ticks = ~4x one recipe cycle, not proven stuck forever). Current file state: inflation.rs has staffing + solar-panel + road-threading + the seller stock=1_000_000 workaround, left exactly as-is per lead ruling, no further probes added.

comments.author: debugger
comments.text: DEBUGGER FINDING: the ToDestination wedge is NOT an itinerary/dispatch-state-machine bug. Confirmed by instrumenting simulation/src/transportation/road.rs::calc_decision/calc_front_dist (reverted, git diff clean): every truck near the factory door (x~126) is permanently speed=0 with a live, valid Route itinerary (never WaitForReroute) blocked by ANOTHER VEHICLE dead ahead (calc_front_dist confirms is_vehicle=true, group=Vehicles every sample). Root: market.rs's Unloading-complete branch (~987) already has a ponytail comment admitting this: 'leave the truck Driving wherever it stopped instead of re-parking... upgrade to RoutingStep::Park... if idle trucks start blocking traffic.' That idle truck sits mid-lane at the factory door forever (Itinerary::NONE, state=Driving, never re-parked), and every subsequent dispatch's truck queues nose-to-tail behind it. The vehicle-vs-vehicle gridlock breaker (Panicking after front_dist<1.5 + flag self-match) never fires in 62k+ ticks (zero 'gridlock!' log lines) because propagation needs the tail vehicle's flag to round-trip through a chain via one-tick-lagged transport_grid_synchronize, and it never converges while new trucks keep queuing behind the permanently-idle one. CONFIRMED by mutation: changed the Unloading-complete branch to cbuf_vehicle.kill(v) instead of ve.it = Itinerary::NONE -- dispatch cycle immediately started completing (dispatches=[] then re-cycling ToSource/ToSource, stock reached upper bound 4, which the unmutated run never did in the sampled window). Mutation reverted. NOT the same defect as sov-jcl (that ticket is about Outbound Loading retry with no route; this is a completed dispatch's truck becoming a permanent physical obstruction). SUGGESTED: implement the RoutingStep::Park spline machinery the comment already names, or at minimum route the truck a short distance off the through-lane to a parking spot before dropping its itinerary.

The dispatches Vec grows without bound and is walked every tick.

(c) IS THE GAMEPLAY-BREAKING ONE: every human bread purchase now creates a Dispatch, but bakeries are kind="store" (base_mod/companies.lua:11,126) and goods_company.rs:129 spawns trucks ONLY `if ckind == CompanyKind::Factory`. VERIFIED. So a city's bakeries accumulate one permanently-reserved dispatch per unfilled meal. Worse: recipe_should_produce reads RAW capital, not capital-reserved, so the bakery also stops producing while holding stock it can never sell.

(a) Loading with no route to buyer (market.rs:520-537): door_pos(buyer) returns None once the buyer's building is demolished; ticks_left is already 0 so it retries forever. The seller was ALREADY debited at ToSource arrival - quantity permanently destroyed. The truck is never dispatcher.free'd (only happens at market.rs:557), so it leaks too.

(b) ToSource with truck: Some(v) where the vehicle entity is gone: world.vehicles.get(v) -> None -> .unwrap_or(false) (market.rs:494-499) -> never arrives. reserved[seller] frozen forever.

FIX: needs a cancellation/timeout path. Consider also whether stores should get trucks, or whether human purchases should create dispatches at all.

PRE-EXISTING - reproduced on an unmodified tree (1 in 5 runs), NOT introduced by ITER-0000.

SYMPTOM: 'cargo test -p simulation' with default parallel threads segfaults intermittently (SIGSEGV, no Rust backtrace - a raw crash, not a panic). Reproduces ~1-in-3 to 1-in-5.

ROOT CAUSE: crate::init::init() (simulation/src/init.rs:33) pushes into 'static mut' INIT_FUNCS / GSYSTEMS / SAVELOAD_FUNCS with no synchronization. Every TestCtx::new() called it unconditionally, so concurrent test threads race on those pushes. rustc already warns here: 'creating a mutable reference to mutable static ... undefined behavior'.

PARTIAL FIX ALREADY IN TREE: TestCtx::new() now guards the init::init() call with std::sync::Once (simulation/src/tests/mod.rs). This REDUCES but does NOT eliminate the crash - some other unsynchronized global path is also involved and was not chased, to respect the do-not-touch-adjacent-code rule.

WORKAROUND until fixed: run 'cargo test -p simulation -- --test-threads=1'. All ITER-0000 verification used it.

WHY P1: the iterative-development spine treats sentinel scenario runs as evidence. A suite that segfaults 1-in-5 produces a confidently wrong signal - a green run proves little and a red run gets blamed on the wrong change. Fix before the sentinel corpus grows.

TRAP: do not 'fix' this by making the tests single-threaded in CI config and calling it done. That hides the UB rather than removing it; the static mut pattern is the defect.","status":"open","priority":1,"issue_type":"bug","created_at":"2026-08-22T15:40:56.339073861Z","created_by":"caio","updated_at":"2026-08-22T15:40:56.339073861Z","source_repo":"soviet-simulator","source_repo_path":"/home/caio/soviet-simulator","compaction_level":0,"original_size":0,"dependency_count":0,"dependent_count":0},{"id":"sov-pillar-assertions-ugb","title":"The design pillars have no runtime assertions","description":"Both pillars were violated in shipped code and no test noticed.

"Nothing teleports" and "never game over" are stated in CLAUDE.md, encoded as prose in ACs, and enforced NOWHERE at runtime.

EVIDENCE: the ext-trade buy block credited a buyer their full requested quantity whenever find_external returned None - which it does whenever world.freight_stations is empty, the normal early game. Every unmatched buy order was granted free, every tick, unpaid, and absent from EcoStats. Scarcity, the entire pressure source of the design, was switched off. It compiled, passed review, and passed every test. Found only when a specialist agent traced conservation across the seam (commit fdfabca).

The conservation invariant in tests/scenarios/ledger.rs is the first assertion of a pillar in the codebase and it only covers quantity.

PROPOSAL: give each pillar a cheap standing assertion the sentinel corpus runs every iteration.
  - nothing teleports: no capital increases without either a completed dispatch unload or a declared production/import source. Generalises ledger.rs beyond a hand-built pair of souls.
  - never game over: no code path terminates a run or produces an unrecoverable state; unmet need must always degrade.
  - clearing by queue, never by price: no Money read gates a physical flow. Partly a grep, better as a runtime assertion.

Cheaper than it sounds and it catches the class of bug that survives code review because the code is correct - it is the DESIGN that is violated.

title: The design pillars have no runtime assertions
description:
Both pillars were violated in shipped code and no test noticed.

"Nothing teleports" and "never game over" are stated in CLAUDE.md, encoded as prose in ACs, and enforced NOWHERE at runtime.

EVIDENCE: the ext-trade buy block credited a buyer their full requested quantity whenever find_external returned None - which it does whenever world.freight_stations is empty, the normal early game. Every unmatched buy order was granted free, every tick, unpaid, and absent from EcoStats. Scarcity, the entire pressure source of the design, was switched off. It compiled, passed review, and passed every test. Found only when a specialist agent traced conservation across the seam (commit fdfabca).

The conservation invariant in tests/scenarios/ledger.rs is the first assertion of a pillar in the codebase and it only covers quantity.

PROPOSAL: give each pillar a cheap standing assertion the sentinel corpus runs every iteration.
  - nothing teleports: no capital increases without either a completed dispatch unload or a declared production/import source. Generalises ledger.rs beyond a hand-built pair of souls.
  - never game over: no code path terminates a run or produces an unrecoverable state; unmet need must always degrade.
  - clearing by queue, never by price: no Money read gates a physical flow. Partly a grep, better as a runtime assertion.

Cheaper than it sounds and it catches the class of bug that survives code review because the code is correct - it is the DESIGN that is violated.

description:
The cheapest guard that would have caught BOTH sov-ledger-exttrade and sov-ledger-remove, per the ledger audit.

title: job-opening reserves stock but never releases it
description:
market.rs:334-336 reserves for EVERY match. market.rs:363 then skips dispatch creation for job-opening (`if kind != ItemID::new("job-opening")`). The dispatch is the ONLY thing that ever decrements `reserved` (market.rs:505) or debits capital (market.rs:503).

So for job-opening: acquire happens, release never does.

Sequence: company C does produce(job_opening, 5) then sell_all (goods_company.rs:166-167). Five humans each buy 1 (human.rs:269). Five matches -> reserved[C] = 5, sell order emptied, but capital[C][job-opening] stays at 5 forever instead of falling to 0.

CURRENTLY SILENT: no production reader of capital(soul, job_opening) outside tests.

LIVE TRAP: any future re-post of the job-opening sell order (rehiring after a worker dies) hits cap_seller - already_reserved = 5 - 5 = 0 < 1, and THE COMPANY CAN NEVER HIRE AGAIN.

FIX: release the reservation immediately for items that get no dispatch, or do not reserve on that branch.

BONUS - false comment: market.rs:358 claims a human buyer owns no building for a truck to route to. human.rs:272 calls set_owner(house, soul), so door_pos DOES resolve for humans. The conclusion (skip dispatch for job-opening) still stands on its other reason, but the stated premise is wrong and will mislead the next editor.
close_reason: commit fdfabca: job-opening debits at match time instead of reserving, since it never gets a dispatch and the dispatch is the only release path. Guard scenario_ledger_job_opening_reserve_leak seen FAILING first (left: 3, right: 0) then passing. Also fixed the false comment about human buyers owning no building (human.rs:272 set_owner).

title: TestCtx determinism check unstable on transport_grid: FnvHashMap serialize order not round-trip-stable
description: Found during sov-lpj fix pass (sim-implementer, 2026-08-26). TestCtx::check_determinism() fails on the transport_grid key with 10 spawned humans over ~20k ticks, holds with 5 humans over 46k. Cause (read from vendored source): TransportGrid = flat_spatial::Grid (transportation/mod.rs:72); flat_spatial-0.6.1 SparseStorage.cells is a fnv::FnvHashMap (storage.rs:31). Bincode serializes HashMap in bucket-iteration order, which is not stable across encode-decode-encode once entries churn — same logical content, different bytes. TRAP: this makes the harness's hash-compare a flaky false-negative source at high entity counts; tests currently dodge it by using fewer humans. Not fixable from test files; needs a BTreeMap-backed storage, a canonical-order serialize wrapper, or excluding transport_grid from the hash.
acceptance_criteria: A test spawning 10+ humans over 20k+ ticks passes check_determinism repeatedly, or transport_grid is excluded from the hash with a comment citing this issue.

title: Extract try_return_to_seller shared by Market::remove and advance_dispatches
description:
Ponytail shrink identified by the opus reviewer on sov-dispatch-wedge-ab4 round 3. The dead-buyer arm of Market::remove (market.rs ~316-368) and the Loading buyer-gone branch of advance_dispatches (~market.rs:872-905) both do the same thing: door_pos(seller) -> Itinerary::route from the truck's position -> on success set the truck's itinerary and transition to Returning, on failure log::warn + dispatcher.free + drop the dispatch. Extracting a shared helper is roughly -45 lines including two comment trims.

DEFERRED DELIBERATELY, not forgotten. Reason (lead ruling 2026-08-26): it is a pure refactor of a conservation-critical function that holds two fresh gate signoffs -- ledger-invariant-checker CONSERVED (which verified Market::remove arm-by-arm and left the file byte-identical) and opus reviewer APPROVE-WITH-FIXES. Re-opening it buys 45 lines against invalidating that baseline, with no behavioural failure driving it.

Do this only when Market::remove is being changed for a real reason anyway, so the gates have to re-run regardless. If you take it: the two sites differ in that advance_dispatches counts return_route_retries against MAX_RETURN_ROUTE_RETRIES and Market::remove does not (it gets one attempt); do not accidentally give the remove path retries it never had, and do not drop the bound from the advance path.
acceptance_criteria: try_return_to_seller extracted and called from both sites; cargo test -p simulation still 42/42 green; the ledger-invariant-checker gate re-run returns CONSERVED; the retry-bound asymmetry between the two call sites is preserved or its change is deliberate and documented.

title: Retail claim-overwrite release is unsound once a second human-purchasable item exists (debug_assert is a release no-op)
description:
market.rs:503-531. When a human's RetailClaim is overwritten, the displaced claim's reservation is released using the per-kind loop's LOCAL 'reserved' map, guarded only by debug_assert_eq!(old.kind, kind) -- which compiles to nothing in release builds.

Sound TODAY only because buyfood.rs:82 is the sole issuer of human buy orders and hardcodes bread, so old.kind always equals kind. The moment a second human-purchasable item exists, an overwrite across kinds silently decrements the WRONG market's reserved row in release builds: one seller's stock is unreserved without cause and another's stays frozen. Silent, no log, invisible to the ledger accountant (it is a reservation defect, not a capital one).

TRIGGER: any change that makes a human buy something other than bread. Fix at that time: look the correct SingleMarket up by old.kind instead of using the loop-local map, and turn the debug_assert into real branching.

Found by ledger-invariant-checker 3rd pass on sov-dispatch-wedge-ab4; explicitly flagged NOT a blocker for that ticket and left latent by lead decision.
acceptance_criteria: Either (a) the release path looks the displaced claim's market up by old.kind rather than relying on the enclosing per-kind loop, with a test that overwrites a claim across two different item kinds and asserts both sellers' reserved rows are correct in a release-semantics build; or (b) a compile-time or runtime invariant makes a cross-kind overwrite impossible and is documented at the call site.

title: Give TestCtx a seed and a fast tick before the journey harness grows
description:
Two gaps found while reviewing the walking-skeleton harness plan.

1. NO SEED. SimulationOptions exposes only terrain_size and save_replay. JOURNEY-0001's final observable claims 'identical seed and inputs yield identical ledger figures', but there is no seed field - today that can only mean 'identical construction'. Either add a seed or reword the observable.

2. TICK COST. TestCtx::tick() does a full bincode encode + decode + per-key hashes() comparison EVERY tick. That is exactly the determinism guarantee we want, but it will dominate runtime on a multi-hundred-tick journey. Add a tick_fast() without the round-trip and keep the checked tick for boundaries.

Not blocking ITER-0000, which is short. Becomes painful as journeys lengthen.

Fast tick added: check_determinism() split out of tick(), advance_ticks(n) checks every 25th tick and always the last. Verified cargo test -p simulation -- --test-threads=1 -> 22 passed.
